# nonInteger

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is **not** an integer.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonInteger() — Checks whether a value is **not** an integer. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/number</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function nonInteger<T>(value: T | number): value is T;
```

`nonInteger(value)` is the same test as `!isInteger(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

A number with no fractional part. Nothing is coerced, so the string `"42"` is not an integer, and `NaN` is not either.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type          | Description         |
| :-------- | :------------ | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `T \| number` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is not an integer; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `T` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
nonInteger(1.5); // => true
nonInteger(NaN); // => true
nonInteger("42"); // => true
nonInteger(42); // => false
nonInteger(-7); // => false
nonInteger(0); // => false
```
